# HarnessDock v0.2.1

This corrected Tauri 2 release supersedes the incomplete v0.2.0 publication path and hardens plugin fault containment across desktop startup paths.

## Key fixes

- Windows x64 ships and resolves Windows-native runtime dependencies only. The retained thin resolver honors npm `os`/`cpu` constraints before downloading, so Windows does not fetch Linux-only native packages.
- Thin first-launch download progress uses the real package completion percentage, while metadata/startup phases are indeterminate instead of showing synthetic progress.
- Thin splash uses the real HarnessDock icon with fixed DPI-safe dimensions and a stable progress layout.
- A plugin/runtime failure is no longer treated as an application-fatal Electron boot error. If dsh cannot start even after compatibility recovery/rollback, HarnessDock keeps its host shell, Diagnostics, tray, update and manual retry controls alive in degraded mode instead of calling `app.quit()`.
- Desktop startup uses bounded plugin compatibility recovery. A normal user profile is attempted first when no valid quarantine exists. After a real startup failure HarnessDock runs boot-free `dsh --dump-config`, separates official/HarnessDock rows from third-party/user rows, records directly implicated rows as suspects, and isolates the complete external set in one recovery boot. This prevents plugin A from failing first and plugin B from failing the retry.
- Recovery never rewrites `cordis.patch.yml` or `$DSH_HOME`. Official `@deepseek-ai/*` rows and HarnessDock's `embedded-client` bridge are excluded from third-party isolation.
- Successful recovery writes an expiring, host-owned plugin quarantine record. It contains plugin IDs/recovery metadata only, is scoped to the exact dsh version, expires after 24 hours by default, and is automatically removed when stale/corrupt or when the dsh version changes. The next launch can therefore avoid reproducing a known plugin crash, while repaired/upgraded configurations receive a fresh normal boot after invalidation/expiry.
- A quarantined boot that fails clears the stale quarantine and retries normal recovery policy instead of trapping the application in a bad safe mode.
- Runtime exposes structured recovery state: recovery source, isolated plugin IDs, suspected plugin IDs, reason and quarantine expiry. Recovery is reported as degraded rather than silently masquerading as fully healthy.
- Runtime crash supervision remains bounded with exponential backoff; repeated crashes stop automatic restart attempts and leave manual recovery controls available.
- `HARNESSDOCK_PLUGIN_RECOVERY=0` disables compatibility retry/quarantine for debugging.
- Linux runtime is glibc-only and removes musl-native variants before AppImage/deb packaging.
- DeepSeek Harness remains pinned to `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1` / `cd5ef8148158c3a752a658978873241fdf8e2bbc`.

## Public platform assets

The public v0.2.1 assets are Tauri-native; legacy Electron installers are not published as v0.2.1 assets.

- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-windows-x64-setup.exe`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.deb`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.AppImage`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-x64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-arm64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.apk`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.aab`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-ios-arm64-simulator.zip`
- Four platform-specific pinned runtime bundles
- `SHA256SUMS`

## Release gate

Publication or same-version replacement requires both the complete `tauri-candidate` matrix and the normal `ci` workflow to succeed for the exact current `main` SHA. The matrix includes Windows NSIS, Linux deb/AppImage, macOS x64/arm64 DMG, Android APK/AAB, iOS simulator archive, four runtime bundles, runtime smoke checks, TypeScript tests on Windows/Linux/macOS, Rust Tauri recovery tests and version consistency checks. An existing v0.2.1 remains available until the replacement candidate is green; only then may the publisher move the tag and overwrite the 13 validated release assets.

## Signing

Public CI packages are build-verified but are not currently Authenticode-signed, Apple-notarized, Google Play-signed, or App Store/TestFlight-provisioned.
